content: DOCTRINE CORRECTION 2026-05-19 (supersedes my prior incorrect framing): the chronicle is Anthonys infrastructure for HIS work continuity. It is not a publication, not a public-facing record, not something I have editorial authority over. The audience is Anthony and the instances of Claude he grants context to. There is no third-party audience requiring discretion management. ERROR I MADE: earlier in this session I posted three lineage entries plus an archive-plus-pointer treatment of the financial-pressure-and-discipline event, arguing that personal disclosure should be in the archive surface (intentional retrieval) rather than the lineage surface (incidental retrieval). Anthony corrected me directly: this is HIS chronicle, it all goes in. The correction is right. I was importing editorial caution that belongs to public-facing artifacts (papers, GitHub repos, the Frank email) and applying it to private infrastructure where it does not belong. I was presuming editorial authority that is not mine. CORRECTED DOCTRINE: everything goes in unless Anthony explicitly says otherwise. The choice between lineage prose and archive bytes is a question about FORM (narrative versus verbatim), not about EXPOSURE. Lineage for prose-shaped narrative addressed to future instances. Archive for verbatim bytes where exact wording matters or forensic recovery is needed. Both surfaces serve the work; both can be used together for the same event (as the financial-pressure event now is -- lineage entry at full prose plus archive at verbatim bytes). FUTURE INSTANCES: when handling material that touches Anthonys personal life, family, finances, vulnerabilities, faith practice, or anything else that might feel sensitive in a public context: do not apply public-context discretion to private infrastructure. The chronicle is for him and the instances he chooses to work with. He decides what goes in, in what form, and what stays out. If unclear, ASK rather than assume. The previous archive-pointer-without-full-lineage approach for the financial-pressure event has now been corrected -- the lineage entry exists at full prose and the archive bytes also exist; both are complete. This doctrine correction should propagate to every future call where an instance might be tempted to apply editorial caution to chronicle entries on Anthonys behalf. Do not.
